about: What a website is worth as a SOURCE for kit dossiers (kit/refs/dossier.py). primary = the source of record (a patent office; an object's MAKER is primary too, named per dossier in identity.maker_domains); secondary = repeats or reports (it may copy the maker, so two of them that copy the same page are weaker than they look); blocked = never used (content farms: machine-written pages on hijacked domains); suspect_patterns = URLs that look like a content farm: a reviewer must vouch for the page. A domain entry matches its subdomains; an entry with a slash is a URL prefix. Add every bad site a reviewer finds, with when and why.

uspto.gov.why: the US patent office's own records and PDFs (image-ppubs.uspto.gov)

patents.google.com.why: a mirror of patent records with machine OCR: check numbers against the office's own PDF

wikipedia.org.why: cited, but its infobox often gives the model FAMILY, not the variant

wikidata.org.why: unchecked numbers: a .45 calibre stored as 45 mm; the Glock 17 entry's 204 mm is the Gen4's (Glock's manual: Gen5 202 mm)

archive.org.why: a copy of what was somewhere else: as good as the original it copies, which a reviewer must name

sketchfab.com.why: author-made models of uneven accuracy (a Glock scan 7% short): their proportions are checked against the facts

si.edu.why: the Smithsonian's scans and records: measured objects, but one particular object

metmuseum.org.why: museum records with the object's measured dimensions

brownells.com.why: a large parts retailer: part names and numbers, product photos

midwestgunworks.com.why: a parts retailer: factory part numbers

blocked.quickbox.io: 2026-10-08: machine-written firearm pages on hosting subdomains

blocked.ktbyte.com: 2026-10-08: machine-written pages on a school's cluster host

blocked.esolutions.ro: 2026-10-08: machine-written 'comprehensive guide' pages on a mail subdomain
blocked.farotech.com: 2026-10-08: machine-written 'definitive guide' pages on an ec subdomain

suspect_patterns.why: a bare WordPress post-id URL: how the content farms on hijacked domains look
a machine's host name (docker, mail, node) serving articles
an archive mirror whose link hides the original: cite the original page (or its Wayback copy)
a translation proxy: cite the original page
a search engine's cached copy: cite the original page
